title: Bispecific Antibodies Market Size, Share & Forecast 2026-2032

market_overview.summary: Published estimates of the bispecific antibody market spread 3.49x at the 2025 base year, from $8.93 billion to $31.17 billion. The explanation is one classification decision: whether non-oncology bispecifics count. Emicizumab and faricimab are bispecific antibodies by construction, and in FY2025 they alone disclosed $10.66 billion of revenue - 74% of all disclosed bispecific revenue and nearly three times every approved oncology bispecific combined. Summing seven disclosed products gives $14.45 billion for FY2025, which this report carries as the 2026 base, reaching $32.90 billion by 2032 at 14.7%.
key_trends: Published 2025 base-year estimates spread 3.49x ($8.93B to $31.17B), and the gap is a definition of the category, not a disagreement about growth
Non-oncology bispecifics are 74% of disclosed revenue: Hemlibra at CHF 4,754 million and Vabysmo at CHF 4,102 million, about $10.66 billion combined
All approved oncology bispecifics we could find disclosed total just $3.79 billion in FY2025, led by Blincyto at $1,559 million
Two published estimates ($8.93B and $10.50B) are below Hemlibra plus Vabysmo alone, so they cannot describe the whole format
One published estimate, Astute Analytica's $14.4 billion for 2025, agrees with the disclosed sum to within 0.3%
The newest T-cell engagers are scaling fast from small bases: Imdelltra reached $627 million in its second full year and Talvey grew 61.3%
market_overview.adoption_level: Established in haemophilia and retinal disease, expanding in haematological oncology

drivers: Two very large non-oncology franchises compounding on a chronic dosing model: Hemlibra grew 11% to CHF 4,754 million in FY2025
Off-the-shelf administration, which lets a T-cell engager reach patients who cannot wait for autologous cell therapy manufacturing
Rapid launch curves in myeloma and small cell lung cancer: Talvey up 61.3% and Imdelltra at $627 million in FY2025
Subcutaneous and fixed-duration regimens, which move administration out of infusion centres
Format maturity - stable, manufacturable IgG-like bispecifics are now a routine engineering choice rather than a research problem
restraints: Step-up dosing and cytokine release syndrome monitoring require inpatient or closely supervised initiation, limiting prescriber reach
Several approved oncology bispecifics compete in the same relapsed/refractory myeloma and lymphoma populations, splitting a fixed pool
Infection risk and prolonged immunosuppression constrain duration of therapy and therefore revenue per patient
Anti-VEGF and haemophilia franchises face biosimilar and gene-therapy competition over the forecast period
Published market sizes are mutually irreconcilable, which makes them unsafe as a planning input
opportunities: Earlier-line movement in lymphoma and myeloma, which multiplies eligible patients without new infrastructure
Non-oncology indications beyond haemophilia and retinal disease, where the format is barely exploited
Combination with antibody-drug conjugates and immunomodulators, raising revenue per patient
Solid tumour targets with a DLL3-like profile, following tarlatamab's commercial proof
challenges: No authoritative public count of approved bispecific antibodies exists; secondary sources give 13 as of late 2024 and 15 as of 2026 on different definitions
Several approved products are not individually disclosed by their owners, so even a careful bottom-up total is a floor
Vendor share cannot be computed, because the denominator itself is unmeasurable from public sources
Class-wide safety management requirements raise the cost of launching each additional product into the same setting

competitive_landscape.market_position: Largest disclosed bispecific revenue, almost entirely non-oncology
competitive_landscape.description: Reported Hemlibra (emicizumab) at CHF 4,754 million for FY2025, up 11% from CHF 4,503 million, and Vabysmo (faricimab) at CHF 4,102 million - together about $10.66 billion at the 2025 annual average rate, or 74% of all bispecific revenue disclosed anywhere. Also markets Columvi and Lunsumio, neither of which Roche breaks out in its FY2025 release. No market share is disclosed.

Reported Blincyto at $1,559 million for FY2025 (US $1,049 million, up 31%; rest of world $510 million, up 23%) and Imdelltra at $627 million including $234 million in the fourth quarter. Blincyto, approved in 2014, remains the single largest disclosed oncology bispecific more than a decade later.

Reported Tecvayli at $670 million for FY2025 (up 22.1% from $549 million) and Talvey at $463 million (up 61.3% from $287 million). Also markets Rybrevant, an EGFR-MET bispecific, which J&J reports jointly with Lazcluze rather than separately, so its annual revenue is not isolable from public disclosure.

Reported global Epkinly/Tepkinly (epcoritamab) net sales of $468 million for FY2025 against $281 million in FY2024, a 67% increase, of which $379 million was booked by Genmab in the US and Japan. Commercialised in partnership with AbbVie, which is paid a profit share.

competitive_landscape.market_position: Partner on an approved lymphoma bispecific
competitive_landscape.description: Shares in Epkinly/Tepkinly economics through its collaboration with Genmab. AbbVie's own disclosure of the product is limited to the profit-share line, which is why this report counts Genmab's global in-market figure once rather than summing both partners.

Markets Lynozyfic (linvoseltamab), among the most recent bispecific approvals. Its revenue is not included in the $14.45 billion aggregate used here, which makes that figure a floor rather than a market total.

regulatory_landscape: FDA Biologics License Application pathway under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act, the route for every approved bispecific antibody
FDA guidance on bispecific antibody development programmes, which sets expectations for characterising each binding arm and the combined construct
FDA accelerated approval pathway, used for several T-cell engagers in relapsed or refractory haematological malignancy and carrying confirmatory trial obligations
Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy programmes applied to T-cell engagers for cytokine release syndrome and neurological toxicity, which determine where therapy may be initiated
EMA centralised marketing authorisation, including conditional authorisation used for bispecifics in relapsed settings
Biosimilar pathways under the Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act, relevant to the large non-oncology franchises over the forecast period

primary_research: No primary interviews were conducted for this edition. This report is a synthesis of audited company disclosures, published third-party estimates and an official exchange rate list, and is labelled as such rather than implying fieldwork that did not occur.
secondary_research: Amgen Form 10-K FY2025 product sales table: Blincyto US $1,049m (+31%) and rest of world $510m (+23%); total product sales $35,148m
Amgen Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 results, February 2026: Imdelltra $627m for the full year, $234m in Q4
Johnson & Johnson FY2025 annual report sales table: Tecvayli $670m (2024 $549m), Talvey $463m (2024 $287m); company sales $94,193m
Genmab 2025 Annual Report: global Epkinly/Tepkinly net sales $468m (2024 $281m), Genmab-booked US and Japan sales $379m
Roche Finance Report 2025 and FY2025 results release of 29 January 2026: Hemlibra CHF 4,754m (+11%), Vabysmo CHF 4,102m, group sales CHF 61.5bn
Swiss Federal Tax Administration 2025 annual average rate of CHF 0.83053 per USD, used for every Roche conversion in this report
Published market estimates from Fortune Business Insights (2025), Astute Analytica (2025), BCC Research, Market Research Future (2025) and Roots Analysis (2025)
research_methodology.data_validation: The headline base is a bottom-up sum of FY2025 disclosed worldwide product revenue for seven approved bispecific antibodies: Blincyto $1,559m, Imdelltra $627m, Tecvayli $670m, Talvey $463m, Epkinly/Tepkinly $468m, plus Hemlibra CHF 4,754m and Vabysmo CHF 4,102m converted at the Swiss Federal Tax Administration 2025 annual average of CHF 0.83053 per USD, giving $5,724m and $4,939m. The total is $14,450m, or $14.45 billion, of which 74% is non-oncology. Rybrevant, Columvi, Lunsumio and Lynozyfic are excluded because their annual revenue is not individually disclosed, so the figure is a floor. The test identifies which published estimates can be product revenue: Roots Analysis's $8.93 billion and Market Research Future's $10.50 billion are both below Hemlibra plus Vabysmo alone and so cannot cover the format, while Fortune Business Insights's $31.17 billion is 2.16x all disclosed bispecific revenue and therefore cannot be product revenue either. Astute Analytica's $14.4 billion agrees with the disclosed sum to within 0.3%, and its 14.7% rate is used for the forecast. This is a plausibility test, not a market estimate, and no methodology behind any published figure was inspected.

faqs.question: How big is the bispecific antibodies market?
faqs.answer: Seven approved bispecific antibodies disclosed $14.45 billion of worldwide revenue in FY2025, and that excludes Rybrevant, Columvi, Lunsumio and Lynozyfic, so it is a floor. This report carries $14.45 billion as the 2026 base and projects $32.90 billion by 2032 at 14.7%. Published 2025 estimates range from $8.93 billion to $31.17 billion.

faqs.question: Why do published estimates differ by 3.49x?
faqs.answer: Because of one classification decision: whether non-oncology bispecifics count. Hemlibra and Vabysmo are bispecific antibodies by construction and disclosed about $10.66 billion between them in FY2025, against $3.79 billion for every approved oncology bispecific we could find. Including or excluding them changes the market by roughly 3.8x, which is close to the observed spread.

faqs.question: Which published estimates can be ruled out?
faqs.answer: Two can be shown not to describe the full format: Roots Analysis's $8.93 billion and Market Research Future's $10.50 billion are both below Hemlibra plus Vabysmo on their own. At the other end, Fortune Business Insights's $31.17 billion is 2.16x all the bispecific revenue anyone discloses, so it cannot be product revenue. Astute Analytica's $14.4 billion matches the disclosed sum to within 0.3%.

faqs.question: Is the oncology side of this market large?
faqs.answer: Not yet. Blincyto at $1,559 million, Imdelltra at $627 million, Tecvayli at $670 million, Talvey at $463 million and Epkinly/Tepkinly at $468 million sum to $3.79 billion for FY2025 - about a quarter of all disclosed bispecific revenue. Growth rates are high, but the absolute base is small.

faqs.question: Who leads the bispecific antibody market?
faqs.answer: Roche, by a wide margin on disclosed revenue, almost entirely from two non-oncology products. Amgen leads in oncology on the strength of Blincyto. No share percentages are published here, because the market denominator is itself a floor derived from incomplete disclosure - any percentage would be a ratio against our own arithmetic.

faqs.question: How many bispecific antibodies are approved?
faqs.answer: No authoritative public count was located. Secondary sources give 13 FDA approvals as of December 2024 and 15 as of 2026, using different definitions of what counts as bispecific. This report names the products individually and quantifies only those whose revenue their owners disclose.

seo.meta_title: Bispecific Antibodies Market Size and Forecast to 2032
seo.meta_description: Published bispecific antibody market sizes spread 3.49x. Disclosed FY2025 revenue of $14.45bn shows the gap is one scope call: do Hemlibra and Vabysmo count?

executive_summary:
Published estimates of the bispecific antibody market put its 2025 size between $8.93 billion and $31.17 billion - a 3.49x spread. The explanation is not vintage, geography or growth. It is a single classification decision that almost no published report states plainly: whether a bispecific antibody counts when it is not an oncology drug.

Emicizumab (Hemlibra) binds factor IXa and factor X. Faricimab (Vabysmo) binds VEGF-A and Ang-2. Both are bispecific antibodies by construction, and in FY2025 Roche reported them at CHF 4,754 million and CHF 4,102 million respectively - about $10.66 billion at the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's 2025 annual average of CHF 0.83053 per USD. Every approved oncology bispecific whose revenue we could find disclosed - Blincyto $1,559 million, Imdelltra $627 million, Tecvayli $670 million, Talvey $463 million, Epkinly/Tepkinly $468 million - sums to $3.79 billion. Non-oncology is therefore 74% of the disclosed total of $14.45 billion, and the two readings of this market differ by roughly 3.8x.

That arithmetic does more than explain the spread; it adjudicates it. Roots Analysis's $8.93 billion and Market Research Future's $10.50 billion are both below Hemlibra plus Vabysmo on their own, so neither can be describing the full format - yet both are more than twice the oncology-only total, so neither matches that reading either. Fortune Business Insights's $31.17 billion is 2.16x every dollar of bispecific revenue anyone discloses, including products we had to leave out of the sum, so it cannot be product revenue. Astute Analytica's $14.4 billion for 2025 agrees with the bottom-up total to within 0.3%, which is why this report uses its growth rate.

The $14.45 billion base is a floor: Rybrevant, Columvi, Lunsumio and Lynozyfic are approved and sold but not individually disclosed. A reader checking any bispecific forecast should start by asking which of these products it counts.
key_highlights: Published 2025 base-year estimates spread 3.49x, from $8.93 billion to $31.17 billion
Seven approved bispecific antibodies disclosed $14.45 billion of FY2025 revenue, 74% of it outside oncology
Hemlibra (CHF 4,754m) and Vabysmo (CHF 4,102m) alone are about $10.66 billion, nearly 3x all approved oncology bispecifics combined
Two published estimates are below Hemlibra plus Vabysmo on their own and so cannot describe the full format
Fortune Business Insights's $31.17 billion is 2.16x all disclosed bispecific revenue, so it cannot be product revenue
Astute Analytica's $14.4 billion for 2025 matches the bottom-up disclosed sum to within 0.3%
The base is a floor: Rybrevant, Columvi, Lunsumio and Lynozyfic are approved but not individually disclosed
market_context:
A bispecific antibody is one molecule with two different binding sites, and that single engineering fact supports two unrelated businesses. In the first, the second binding arm replaces a missing biological bridge: emicizumab substitutes for activated factor VIII by holding factor IXa and factor X together, turning a haemophilia A patient's intravenous regimen into a subcutaneous one. In the second, the second arm recruits a killer - a CD3 bispecific grabs a T cell with one hand and a tumour antigen with the other, forcing a synapse that would not otherwise form.

These have almost nothing in common commercially. The haemophilia and retinal products are chronic, outpatient, prescribed by non-oncologists and measured in years of therapy per patient. The T-cell engagers are fixed-duration or until-progression, initiated under supervision because of cytokine release syndrome, and concentrated in relapsed or refractory haematological malignancy where the eligible pool is small and already crowded.

That is why a market sized as 'bispecific antibodies' is sensitive to a definition rather than to the economy. It is also why the oncology side looks disappointing in absolute terms despite excellent growth rates: Blincyto was approved in 2014 and is still the largest disclosed oncology bispecific at $1,559 million, while newer entrants such as Imdelltra and Talvey are growing from bases in the hundreds of millions. The format is proven; the commercial scale is still mostly in non-oncology.
forecast_analysis:
The series starts at $14.45 billion for 2026 - the FY2025 disclosed revenue of seven approved bispecific antibodies, carried forward unchanged because 2026 revenue is not yet disclosed - and compounds at 14.7% to $32.90 billion by 2032. The intermediate years are interpolation on that single rate.

The rate is Astute Analytica's published 2026-2035 figure, chosen for a specific reason: Astute's own published base of $14.4 billion for 2025 is the only one that reconciles with the bottom-up disclosed total. Using a rate from a house whose base our arithmetic rules out would be mixing an audited level with a slope derived from a different market.

The composition of that growth is the part to watch. Roughly three-quarters of the base is two mature franchises growing in the high single digits - Hemlibra grew 11% in FY2025 - and facing biosimilar and gene-therapy pressure later in the period. The high-growth quarter is oncology, where Talvey grew 61.3% and Imdelltra reached $627 million in its second full year, but from bases small enough that even excellent percentage growth adds limited absolute revenue before 2030. A forecast above the mid-teens therefore requires either earlier-line oncology labels or a second non-oncology franchise of Hemlibra's scale, and should name which.
reader_takeaways: Before using any bispecific antibody forecast, check whether it counts Hemlibra and Vabysmo - that one decision moves the market by roughly 3.8x
Two of the five mainstream published estimates are below Hemlibra plus Vabysmo alone, so they cannot be describing the whole format
The oncology side is only about a quarter of disclosed revenue: high growth rates on small absolute bases
Treat any vendor share percentage as unsourced - even a careful bottom-up total is a floor, because several approved products are not individually disclosed
Model the non-oncology franchises for biosimilar and gene-therapy pressure late in the period, not for indefinite compounding
